analysis:
The only changed file is docs/developer/build.md: a date bump (line 3), a new interim-size paragraph (head lines 622-633), and a CI lane-size table rewrite (head lines 666-679). The change is documentation of CI runner sizing: production signs only 8x16 and 12x32, so most lanes temporarily ask for 8x16 and test-cluster-gpu-2 asks for 12x32. It records that 4x16 and 4x24 returned shape_not_signed.

I found no change to provider code, the coordinator-to-provider WebSocket contract (TB-002), the attestation or App Attest paths (TB-009, TB-011), keys (A-002, A-003), cache encryption (T-041), or the add-on, sandbox and GPU-limit boundaries (TB-012, TB-013, TB-014). Nothing in the diff alters any threat-model asset, trust boundary, assumption or mitigation. No threat-model update is needed.

The surrounding unchanged text (CI routing, cache gating, sparse checkout, .git hook sanitization) was read for context. The edits only describe fallback and size selection, and the fallback behavior that keeps jobs off Darkbloom when the plane lacks a signed size is unchanged. The one limit on this review is that the actual workflow files (provider-plan.yml, scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py) are not in this batch. I therefore cannot confirm the doc matches the code, but a mismatch would be a documentation or availability issue rather than a security regression. The patch excerpt is truncated, but the head text was fully visible for the changed ranges.
